data.title: ‘Al Shannah Day’ Event Attracts Locals and Visitors in AlUla
data.content:
AlUla, November 21, 2026, SPA -- The “Al Shannah Day” event, held today at Al Manshiyah Farmers’ Market as part of the “Khairat AlUla” season, attracted residents and visitors with live demonstrations of the traditional method of preserving dates using Al Shannah, a time-honored practice passed down through generations in the region.
    Experienced locals showed how to prepare Al Shannah and fill it with dates, explaining each stage of the process, from selecting and cleaning the fruit to packing and compressing it to eliminate air pockets before securely stitching the container closed. Al Shannah is made from tanned and cleaned sheep or goat hides and was long used to store dates while maintaining their quality for extended periods.
    The Al Shannah is closely associated with traditional hospitality, as hosts would open one to serve dates to their guests. It continues to be used on various occasions and during different seasons, including Ramadan, remaining an integral part of AlUla's agricultural and social heritage, which is closely linked to palm trees and date cultivation in its oases.
    The initiative falls within the Royal Commission for AlUla's efforts to safeguard tangible and intangible cultural heritage, raise awareness of it, and hand it down to future generations. Held during the autumn break, it offered residents and visitors an opportunity to learn about this heritage practice, underscoring the commitment of AlUla's youth to upholding the tradition and sharing the knowledge associated with it.
    -- SPA
